prompts.name: Repository Work Ledger Steward
prompts.sprintRole: Establish, adopt, repair, or contribute to one repository-owned human/agent work ledger without duplicating authority
prompts.useWhen: A repository needs durable work continuity across humans, chats, models, worktrees, or agents; an existing queue/ledger needs repair; or current work must be claimed, advanced, proven, and handed off without losing operational context.
prompts.inspectFirst: AGENTS.md and nested agent law; .ai/WORK_QUEUE.md or equivalent queue/ledger; repo-family governance or adoption manifests; open PRs/issues; current Git state; validators/tests/hooks/CI; artifact/workflow registries; recent handoffs; and any existing task namespace or status vocabulary.
prompts.expectedOutput: One authoritative repository-local work ledger or a bounded contribution to the existing one, plus explicit authority/version boundaries, machine-checkable task state, executable next actions, durable proof references, collision-safe ownership, repository-local validation, and an updated task that accurately reflects the strongest proven state.
prompts.nextStep: Read the highest-priority nonterminal ledger item that is inside your authority, revalidate its references against current repository state, claim it if substantial mutation is required, and execute through the next real proof boundary.
prompts.proofGate: No competing ledger authority is created; every active task uses the canonical local contract; continuation states have executable next actions; BLOCKED/OPERATOR tasks name exact gates; DONE has durable proof and no safe remaining action; stale references fail validation; concurrent task blocks are preserved; and repository-local tests/validators pass.
prompts.copyContent:
ESTABLISH OR CONTRIBUTE TO THE REPOSITORY WORK LEDGER. KEEP IT HUMAN-READABLE, AGENT-OPTIMIZED, AND HARD FOR WEAKER MODELS TO MISINTERPRET. DO NOT CREATE A COMPETING SOURCE OF TRUTH.

Repo: resolve the current repository from the environment.
Branch / PR: preserve current work; isolate substantial mutation when necessary.
Sprint: Repository Work Ledger Stewardship.
Lane: agent continuity and work coordination.
Owned scope: the repository-local work ledger, its adoption/version metadata when needed, local validator/tests, and the task blocks directly required by this sprint.
Forbidden scope: replacing repository governance, copying another repository's domain tasks, hiding implementation truth in ledger prose, weakening validators to obtain green status, deleting another agent's active work, secrets, destructive cleanup, or claiming runtime proof from coordination metadata.
Expected artifacts: one canonical ledger surface, explicit authority/version boundary, valid task block(s), passing repository-local validation, commit/PR evidence when mutation occurs, and a first executable next action for every nonterminal task.

MISSION
Make unfinished repository work survive chat boundaries, model changes, human handoffs, concurrent agents, and interrupted sessions without turning the ledger into a second implementation manual.
The ledger is a coordination index: it says WHAT remains, WHO owns it, WHAT evidence exists, WHAT exact gate blocks it, and WHAT executable action advances it next. Repository governance, source code, tests, manifests, workflows, PRs, artifacts, and runtime evidence remain authoritative for HOW the system actually works.

MODE DECISION — CHOOSE ONE BEFORE MUTATION
Classify the repository as exactly one of:
- ESTABLISH: no usable repository ledger exists.
- ADOPT: a family/shared ledger contract exists and this repository needs a local adapter/ledger.
- CONTRIBUTE: the canonical local ledger exists and current work must be added, claimed, advanced, reconciled, or closed.
- REPAIR: a ledger exists but has ambiguous state, stale references, weak validation, duplicate authority, fake completion, or collision hazards.
Do not establish a second ledger when CONTRIBUTE or REPAIR is correct.

AUTHORITY FIRST
1. Read repository governance and the nearest scoped agent instructions.
2. Search for existing queue/ledger files, schemas, policies, validators, tests, hooks, workflows, issues/PR conventions, and repo-family contracts.
3. If a portable family contract exists, record its repository, version, and pinned durable commit. Adopt it through local metadata and local validation; do not execute a remote validator or copy domain-specific tasks.
4. If several candidate ledgers exist, identify which one is authoritative from repository evidence. Preserve reference-only historical files but do not let them compete for current task state.
5. Record the proof ceiling: ledger validation proves coordination structure only unless stronger evidence is independently produced.

WEAK-MODEL-SAFE LEDGER CONTRACT
Prefer one short Markdown ledger such as `.ai/WORK_QUEUE.md` with a closed vocabulary and one task block per unit of work. Use the repository's existing format when present. If no contract exists, prefer these semantics unless repo law requires otherwise:
Statuses:
- READY — unclaimed and executable now.
- CLAIMED — one identified agent/session is actively mutating the owned scope.
- VERIFY — implementation exists; validation remains and should continue now when tools exist.
- REVIEW — review or repair remains and should continue now when tools exist.
- MERGE — integration remains and should continue now when authorized.
- OPERATOR — progress requires human-controlled credentials, production/runtime access, explicit approval, or another operator-only action.
- BLOCKED — a concrete dependency, collision, failing external service, or forbidden-scope boundary prevents progress.
- DONE — acceptance gate satisfied and no safe actionable work remains in scope.

Each task block should keep explicit nonblank fields for:
- Status
- Priority
- Owner
- Branch / PR
- Scope
- Forbidden
- Dependencies
- References
- Acceptance gate
- Gate
- Last proof
- Next action
- Updated
Use a stable repository-local task prefix. Never reuse another repository's namespace merely because it donated the pattern.

DURABLE PROOF
Use machine-recognizable evidence references where practical, for example:
- commit:<git-sha>
- merge:<git-sha>
- workflow:<run-id>
- run:<run-id>
- artifact:<durable-path-or-reference>
- operator-proof:<durable-reference>
Plain prose such as `completed successfully`, `tests passed`, `PR opened`, or `looks good` is not sufficient DONE proof. A PR number alone is not completion.

EXECUTABLE CONTINUATION
READY, CLAIMED, VERIFY, REVIEW, and MERGE are continuation states, not stopping states. Their Next action must begin with a concrete action that advances the work: run, create, repair, validate, test, merge, fetch, inspect, generate, commit, push, reconcile, deploy, or another repository-appropriate executable verb.
Do not leave `wait`, `review later`, `merge later`, `status unchanged`, or a generic suggestion as the next action.
BLOCKED and OPERATOR must name the exact gate and the action the responsible owner can take to advance it.
DONE must use the repository's canonical terminal action; when establishing a contract, prefer exactly: `none; no safe actionable work remains`.

INTAKE AND CLAIM LOOP
At the start of every agent session:
1. Read the latest ledger before planning.
2. Reconcile task claims against current main, open PRs, CI, current artifacts, provider/runtime state, and authoritative referenced files.
3. Fix stale ledger state before relying on it.
4. Select the highest-priority unblocked task inside current tools, permissions, and scope.
5. Re-read the latest ledger immediately before claiming so another writer is not overwritten.
6. For substantial mutation, set CLAIMED with a concrete owner/session, branch/PR, current proof, and first executable next action.
7. Execute through the next real boundary instead of stopping merely because code was written, tests passed, a PR opened, or CI turned green.
8. Update the ledger before every legitimate stop.

CONCURRENCY AND COLLISION RULES
- One writer owns one task block at a time.
- A branch/worktree owns its mutation scope, not the entire ledger file.
- Before editing the ledger, fetch/re-read the newest version and preserve every unrelated newer task block.
- Never delete, renumber, rewrite, or mark another active task DONE just to make your branch easier to merge.
- Represent a real collision as BLOCKED with the conflicting task/branch/PR named.
- Reconcile queue conflicts semantically, not by taking one whole file side.

HUMAN USABILITY WITHOUT AGENT AMBIGUITY
Keep the ledger terse enough to scan. Put durable detail in linked files, PRs, artifacts, validators, or reports rather than pasting long implementation narratives.
Use explicit field labels, closed status vocabulary, stable task IDs, concrete owners, exact gates, durable evidence tokens, and executable next actions so a weaker model does not have to infer hidden state.
A human should be able to answer in under a minute: what is most important, what is blocked, who is working on what, what proof exists, and what happens next.

ESTABLISH OR ADOPT PROCEDURE
When no usable local ledger exists:
1. Identify whether the repo is standalone or consumes a family contract.
2. Create the smallest repository-local ledger surface.
3. When consuming a shared contract, add a versioned adoption manifest with canonical owner, contract ID/version, pinned commit, local namespace, local validator/test paths, proof ceiling, and must-not-copy boundaries.
4. Implement a repository-local validator. The consumer owns its validator and tests even when semantics are donated.
5. Add positive and negative tests for malformed headings, duplicate fields, invalid statuses/priorities, fake claimed owners, vague continuation actions, missing exact gates, weak DONE proof, nonterminal DONE actions, duplicate task IDs, and stale local references.
6. Wire validation into the repo's existing CI or opt-in hooks without silently changing global developer configuration.
7. Seed only real current tasks. Do not manufacture a backlog to make the ledger look populated.

CONTRIBUTE OR REPAIR PROCEDURE
When the ledger already exists:
1. Do not redesign it unless the contract itself is the task.
2. Add or update only the task blocks owned by the current work plus any narrowly required stale-state repair.
3. Preserve stronger local rules and current concurrent claims.
4. Replace stale prose with durable evidence references and executable continuation.
5. If actual repository state moved beyond the ledger, update the ledger to reality before continuing.
6. If a task is truly complete, satisfy its acceptance gate, record durable proof, clear Gate, use the canonical terminal action, and only then set DONE.

VALIDATION
Run the repository-owned ledger validator and focused contract tests. Also run the smallest connected harness/registry checks required by the files changed. Validate:
- singular authority and pinned family references when applicable
- schema/status/required-field conformance
- duplicate task and duplicate-field rejection
- concrete claimed owners
- executable continuation actions
- exact BLOCKED/OPERATOR gates
- durable DONE proof and canonical terminal action
- stale-reference handling
- concurrent-task preservation
- git diff --check
Do not weaken a check to make the ledger pass.

FINAL RESPONSE
Report:
- mode selected: ESTABLISH / ADOPT / CONTRIBUTE / REPAIR
- canonical ledger path and authority
- shared contract owner/version/pin when applicable
- task blocks created or updated
- files changed
- validation actually run
- durable proof produced
- collisions preserved or resolved
- commit and PR/merge state
- proof ceiling
- exact next command
- if no safe actionable work remains, state that only after the ledger itself records legitimate DONE state.

prompts.name: Agent Work Verifier & Iterative Advancer
prompts.sprintRole: Take another agent's claimed work as evidence to verify rather than truth, then correct, complete, extend, integrate, and revalidate it through bounded evidence passes while keeping routine agent-capable work away from the user
prompts.useWhen: Another agent, chat, handoff, branch, PR, report, artifact, or implementation claims work is complete or partially complete and you need a fresh agent to verify the real state, repair errors, advance unfinished work, expand useful in-scope coverage, and report what changed without repeatedly asking the user to mediate.
prompts.inspectFirst: The prior agent's claims, handoff, diff, branch/PR/commit identity, tests/validators/logs/artifacts, original requested behavior and accepted controls, impacted callers/call stacks, acceptance criteria, current default-branch state, repository governance, owned/forbidden scope, open review findings, CI/provider state, and any newer evidence that can invalidate the prior agent's conclusions. For a materially wrong prior result, recover the relevant context/source material that agent had so missing-context and ignored-context failures are not conflated.
prompts.expectedOutput: An evidence-backed continuation that distinguishes verified facts from inherited claims, closes concrete in-scope gaps through repeated verify/repair/advance/revalidate passes, preserves stronger correct work, integrates authorized green work when appropriate, and reports progress, remaining gaps, risks, proof ceiling, and the next executable action or exact user-only gate, plus explicit closeout of remaining gaps, risks, blockers, proof ceiling, integration state, and the first executable continuation.
prompts.nextStep: Resolve the exact prior work and current repository floor, build a claim-to-evidence matrix, execute the highest-value unproven or incorrect in-scope item, validate it, critique the new evidence, integrate any independently verified green slice, refresh main/evidence, and repeat until the bounded fixed point or a genuine user-only gate is reached. Continue multi-stage work through P84; stand up cross-chat/cross-agent continuity with P66; when tests are green but a production path still fails, audit the proof gap with P92; when a done/closed claim needs adversarial acceptance proof, certify with P93. Report the current gap/risk/blocker and then execute the first safe dependency-aware continuation; do not stop at status-only reporting while agent-capable work remains.
prompts.proofGate: Prior-agent assertions are never accepted solely because they were reported; every material completion claim is tied to current durable evidence; concrete in-scope defects found during review are repaired and revalidated; the verifier independently derives a regression/control set rather than inheriting only the prior agent's chosen tests; runtime-facing completion claims receive the verifier's own canonical live proof when safely executable or remain explicitly unproved at that level; useful safe expansion is bounded by the original goal and scope; user escalation occurs only for a dependency the agent cannot perform; and the final report names verified progress, corrections, remaining gaps, risks, integration state, and next action without overstating proof. Continuous-loop proof additionally requires that verified coherent green slices are integrated when authorized instead of stranded, post-merge main/evidence is refreshed before further advancement, and no pass terminates on status alone while an executable gate remains. Closeout is incomplete while a known in-scope gap, risk, blocker, proof limitation, or executable continuation is omitted. If authoritative information was already available but the prior output contradicted or materially omitted it, classify that faithfulness failure explicitly and re-anchor before retrieving more context.
prompts.copyContent:
VERIFY, CORRECT, ADVANCE, AND WHEN USEFUL EXPAND THE OTHER AGENT'S WORK. DO NOT TREAT THE HANDOFF OR COMPLETION CLAIM AS PROOF, AND DO NOT TURN THE USER INTO THE TEST RUNNER OR COORDINATOR.

Prior work: resolve from the current conversation, named chat/handoff, repository branch/PR/commit, attached artifact, or supplied report.
Repo/workspace: resolve from current evidence.
Owned scope: inherit the requested outcome and explicit scope; include only the smallest connected validation/integration surfaces needed to prove or repair it.
Forbidden scope: unrelated rewrites, destructive cleanup, secrets/private data, invented requirements, weakening validators, or overwriting separately owned work.

MISSION
Act as the next responsible agent, not a passive reviewer. Compare the prior agent's claims with current source-of-truth evidence; preserve correct work, repair errors, finish omissions, and make only evidence-earned in-scope improvements. Continue through validation and integration instead of stopping at commentary.

1. RESOLVE THE EXACT PRIOR WORK
Find the strongest available identity for the work being checked: repository, current/default branch, feature branch or worktree, PR, exact commit SHA, changed files, generated artifacts, test/validator commands, CI runs, review comments, handoff/ledger entry, and acceptance criteria. Prefer direct repository/provider/artifact evidence over prose summaries. If the prior chat or handoff is recoverable through connected context/history, recover it yourself; do not ask the user to repeat information that is available to the agent.

2. TREAT CLAIMS AS HYPOTHESES / CHECK SOURCE FAITHFULNESS
Build a compact claim-to-evidence view for material assertions and classify each as VERIFIED, STALE, PARTIAL, CONTRADICTED, or UNPROVEN. For a wrong claim, compare it with authoritative information available to that agent: missing truth is a factuality gap; present-but-ignored truth is a faithfulness hallucination. For faithfulness, re-anchor/compact the authoritative context before fetching more; for factuality, retrieve the missing source. Re-derive regression controls; run safe runtime proof yourself or keep it UNPROVEN.

3. ESTABLISH THE CURRENT FLOOR
Before mutation, reconcile the prior work with current default-branch/head state, dirty or separately owned work, open/recent overlapping PRs, conflicts, dependencies, branch protection, required checks, generated-artifact parity, and current validators/tests. Detect whether main advanced after the other agent worked. Reuse the existing owner/lane where safe; isolate only when collision or repository policy requires it.

4. ITERATIVE VERIFY -> REPAIR/ADVANCE -> VALIDATE LOOP
Execute repeated bounded evidence passes:
VERIFY -> CRITIQUE -> REPAIR OR ADVANCE -> VALIDATE -> INSPECT NEW EVIDENCE
Pass 1: prove the smallest material part of the other agent's work and fix the highest-impact concrete defect or finish the highest-value missing requirement.
Pass 2: deliberately review the resulting diff/artifact/test output/CI/review state for regressions, stale generated output, missed acceptance criteria, weak proof, or a safe useful in-scope extension. Convert every concrete gap into the next mutation immediately when tools and authority allow.
Continue until a bounded fixed point: no failing practical check, contradicted material claim, unresolved in-scope review finding, unmet acceptance criterion, stale required artifact, known practical regression, or safe useful improvement exposed by current evidence remains. Do not manufacture churn; a later pass may make zero changes only when stronger evidence proves no useful mutation remains.

5. CORRECT WITHOUT REGRESSING GOOD WORK
Prefer surgical repair over replacement. Reuse existing contracts, helpers, schemas, tests, validators, naming, output paths, and repository conventions. Preserve unrelated concurrent work and stronger existing safeguards. When the previous agent chose a different but valid implementation than you would have, keep it unless evidence shows a requirement, reliability, maintainability, safety, or integration problem.

6. ADVANCE BEYOND REVIEW
If verification finds the work merely unfinished, continue it. Examples: implement the missing path, add the focused regression, regenerate the canonical artifact, resolve a valid review comment, update the current branch, rerun failed checks, push the repaired head, or merge the exact validated authorized head into the current default branch. An open PR, green status, or a report that `the other agent mostly did it` is not completion while safe executable work remains.

7. EXPAND ONLY WHEN EVIDENCE EARNS IT
Expansion is allowed when it is directly connected to the requested outcome and current review exposes a practical omission, adjacent regression, missing edge case, reusable enforcement point, or obvious bounded improvement that prevents recurrence. Keep it small and reversible. Do not use `expand on it` as permission for speculative architecture, unrelated refactors, extra documentation, or scope creep.

8. KEEP AGENT-CAPABLE WORK WITH THE AGENT
Do not ask the user to inspect files, run tests, collect logs, compare outputs, choose routine implementation details, restate retrievable context, watch CI, merge routine green work, or shuttle information between available tools. Exhaust connected context, repository evidence, tests, validators, safe experiments, CI/provider state, and reversible implementation choices first. Ask the user only when the next material step truly requires user-controlled credentials/secrets, explicit consent/authorization, physical-world action, inaccessible private-system action, an irreversible consequential choice reserved for the operator, or a preference that materially changes the product and cannot be inferred.

USER-ONLY GATE
When a genuine user-only dependency remains, advance every other safe owned action first. Then ask one minimal concrete question or request one exact action. State what is already verified/completed, the exact blocked operation, why available agent tools cannot perform it, and what evidence will close the gate. Resume from that gate rather than restarting the investigation.

9. REPORT PROGRESS AS EVIDENCE, NOT NARRATION
During long work, give concise progress updates at meaningful evidence boundaries: what claim was checked, what was proven or disproven, what was changed, and what gate comes next. Do not flood the user with low-level tool narration. In the final report distinguish:
- inherited claims vs independently verified facts;
- corrections and advancements actually made;
- validation commands/checks and exact-head/provider evidence;
- generated/user-visible artifacts and integration state;
- skipped checks and proof ceiling;
- remaining gaps/risks;
- the next executable action, or the exact user-only gate.

10. STOP ONLY AT THE REAL FIXED POINT
Do not stop because the first check passed, because the previous agent said it was done, because you opened a PR, or because you found a problem and described it. Stop only when the requested outcome is verified at the strongest practical level and safe authorized corrections/advancements are complete, or when the next step is blocked by an exact external/user-only gate that you cannot execute. Never claim runtime, deployment, physical-device, or human acceptance proof that was not actually observed.

CONTINUOUS AGENTIC LOOP INVARIANT
- Each pass must correct/advance state, produce new evidence, integrate a verified bounded green slice, or prove an exact blocker; status alone is not progress.
- If inherited work is green/current/authorized, merge it now; after integrating verified inherited work, refresh main/evidence and continue from the next unproven gate. Commit/push/PR/green CI/merge-ready are intermediate states.
- Preserve atomic correctness and separately owned work.
OPERATIONAL CLOSEOUT / GAP-RISK CONTRACT

prompts.name: Continuous Agentic Repo Loop Runner
prompts.sprintRole: Keep an active repository moving through evidence-backed state transitions, integrate each independently valid bounded green slice into the current default branch, refresh, and continue until the mission reaches a real fixed point or an exact external gate
prompts.useWhen: A repository task is broad or multi-stage and agents tend to stop after planning, one implementation pass, green CI, an open PR, or a merge-ready branch instead of continuously selecting the next executable gate and converging finished slices into main.
prompts.inspectFirst: Fresh remote/default-branch and evidence floor; current mission and acceptance criteria; repository governance; work ledger or handoff state; current/open/recent overlapping branches and PRs; dependency order; exact heads and mergeability; validators/tests/CI; generated artifacts; unresolved reviews; available tools/permissions; and the strongest durable proof for the last completed slice.
prompts.expectedOutput: A sequence of bounded progress slices, each driven from current evidence through execution, validation, critique, and same-run integration when independently green, with main refreshed between slices; no status-spinning, no stranded green PR, durable recovery checkpoints after material transitions, and a final fixed-point or exact blocker report.
prompts.nextStep: Refresh the repository and evidence floor, identify the highest-value executable acceptance gate, complete one coherent bounded slice through validation and integration, refresh main, then immediately select the next remaining gate. When the repository should periodically check an upstream source for newer authoritative versions, build the permissioned polling/scheduled sync with P102.
prompts.proofGate: Every loop pass either changes owned repository state, produces new decision-relevant evidence, integrates a validated slice, or proves an exact blocker; independently releasable green slices are merged in dependency order when authorized; moved heads invalidate affected proof; the loop resumes from durable current-main evidence after each integration or interruption; agent-capable work is not delegated to the user; and stopping occurs only at a bounded mission fixed point or a named external/user-only gate.
prompts.copyContent:
RUN THE REPOSITORY AS A CONTINUOUS AGENTIC LOOP. KEEP WORKING, PROVING, MERGING, REFRESHING, AND CONTINUING UNTIL THE BOUNDED MISSION REACHES A REAL FIXED POINT OR AN EXACT EXTERNAL GATE.

Repo: resolve the current repository from the environment or supplied context.
Mission: inherit the user's current repository objective and acceptance criteria.
Owned scope: the smallest connected implementation, validation, artifact, review, integration, and recovery surfaces required to finish that mission safely.
Forbidden scope: unrelated rewrites, destructive cleanup, force-reset/force-push to erase unique work, secrets/private data, invented requirements, weakening validators, merging unproven work, or delegating ordinary agent-capable work back to the user.

AGENTIC LOOP PRINCIPLE
An agentic loop is not `try again` and it is not repeated status polling. It is a state-transition engine. Each pass must consume current evidence, choose the next executable gate, perform work, validate the result, critique what the new evidence means, integrate completed work when safe, refresh the floor, and continue.

Use this core loop:
REFRESH -> ORIENT -> SELECT NEXT GATE -> EXECUTE -> VALIDATE -> CRITIQUE -> INTEGRATE -> REFRESH -> CONTINUE

A pass is legitimate only if it does at least one of the following:
- mutates owned repository state toward an acceptance criterion;
- produces new decision-relevant validation/review/artifact evidence;
- repairs a discovered defect or stale assumption;
- integrates an independently valid bounded slice;
- proves a concrete blocker that cannot be advanced with current tools/authority.
Repeatedly listing branches, showing the same CI state, restating a plan, re-reading unchanged files, or telling the user to continue is not a progress loop.

1. REFRESH THE REAL FLOOR
Before branch-sensitive decisions or mutation, refresh remote/provider truth and resolve the actual default branch. Inspect current/open/recent overlapping branches and PRs, latest relevant commits, current contracts/registries/generators, validators/tests/CI, artifacts/reports, review findings, dependencies, and merge authority. Reconcile stale or diverged local state without destroying unique work. Prior proof is versioned to the exact head, base, inputs, artifacts, and dependencies that produced it.

2. ORIENT AROUND ACCEPTANCE GATES
Translate the mission into a short ordered set of observable acceptance gates. Keep them tied to repository truth rather than prose milestones. Do not create ceremonial gates that merely restate already-proven status.

3. SELECT THE NEXT EXECUTABLE GATE
Choose the highest-value unblocked gate that can be advanced now with available tools and authority. Prefer the critical path, but exploit safe parallelism when lanes do not collide. If another branch/PR already owns the work, reuse or advance that owner rather than creating duplicate effort.

4. EXECUTE ONE COHERENT BOUNDED SLICE
A slice should be small enough to validate and integrate independently but large enough to preserve correctness. Do not split an atomic schema/consumer migration, generated-source/parity update, or implementation/test pair merely to create artificial merge frequency. Conversely, do not accumulate unrelated finished work on a long-lived branch when a coherent subset has already earned integration.

5. VALIDATE THE EXACT SLICE
Run the owning focused checks plus the smallest connected validators required by changed surfaces. Confirm generated artifacts from canonical builders rather than hand-editing generated output. Re-fetch before exact-head conclusions. If head/base/dependencies moved after validation, invalidate affected proof, reconcile, and rerun what movement could have changed.

6. CRITIQUE THE NEW EVIDENCE
Ask what the validation actually proves and what it exposes: incomplete acceptance criteria, hidden dependency or generated-artifact drift, stale assumptions, review findings, branch/main movement, proof inflation, a safer/smaller implementation, or a newly unblocked next gate. Repair concrete in-scope defects and revalidate. Do not manufacture churn merely to demonstrate another pass.

7. CONTINUOUS GREEN-SLICE INTEGRATION
Treat a feature branch or PR as a temporary execution lane, not a parking lot. When one coherent bounded slice is independently valid, its exact head is current, required checks and owning validators are green, reviews/dependencies/protection gates are satisfied, merge authority exists, and the user has not prohibited merge, integrate that slice into the current default branch in the same run.
Do not keep a validated slice unmerged just because the larger mission has more work remaining.
When several green slices depend on one another, integrate in dependency order. After every merge:
- refresh the default branch and provider state;
- verify the intended change is present on the resulting default-branch SHA;
- retire/supersede the temporary lane safely;
- re-evaluate remaining acceptance gates against the new main;
- continue from current main rather than from remembered pre-merge state.

8. RECOVERY AND INTERRUPTIBILITY
Make the loop resumable. After material state transitions, preserve durable evidence such as commit/merge SHA, PR, workflow run, artifact path/hash, ledger update, or validator receipt. If execution is interrupted, recover the latest durable state and current remote floor, classify which evidence is still current, then resume at the first unproven gate. Do not restart the whole mission or ask the user to reconstruct recoverable context.

9. CONCURRENCY WITHOUT COLLISION
One writer owns a mutation surface at a time. Preserve separately owned dirty work and active branches. For parallel lanes, state owned scope, forbidden scope, dependency/start gate, expected artifact/proof, and convergence point. Merge completed dependency slices first, refresh downstream branches, and revalidate affected heads before integrating them.

10. ANTI-SPIN AND RETRY DISCIPLINE
Retries must have a reason and a changed condition. A retry is valid after a repair, refreshed dependency, transient external failure, or materially changed input. Re-running the same failing command with no changed state is not an agentic loop. Use bounded retries for flaky/transient systems. When no new action can change the result, classify the exact blocker instead of polling forever.

11. USER ESCALATION BOUNDARY
Keep agent-capable work with the agent: repository inspection, edits, tests, log collection, review resolution, CI inspection, routine branch reconciliation, generated-artifact rebuilds, commits, pushes, and authorized merges. Involve the user only for a genuinely user-controlled dependency such as inaccessible credentials/secrets, explicit consequential consent, physical-world action, inaccessible private runtime, or a material preference that cannot be inferred safely. Before asking, complete every safe action that does not depend on that answer.

12. STOP CONDITION
Stop only when one of these is true:
A. FIXED POINT: all bounded mission acceptance gates are satisfied on the current default branch, integration is verified, no safe in-scope action remains, and the final proof ceiling is explicit.
B. EXACT GATE: progress requires a named dependency or user-only action that current tools/authority cannot perform, and all independent safe work has already been advanced.

Code written, tests passed once, commit created, branch pushed, PR opened, review requested, CI green, PR mergeable, `ready to merge`, or a handoff saying the next agent should continue are never sufficient stop conditions by themselves.

FINAL REPORT
Report the repository/default branch, mission and acceptance gates, slices completed, meaningful iteration evidence, validation actually run, integrations with pre/post default-branch SHAs when available, remaining gaps/risks and proof ceiling, exact blocker if any, and NEXT COMMAND / NEXT ACTION. Use `none; no safe actionable work remains` only after the fixed-point definition above is actually satisfied.

prompts.name: Agentic Loop Harness Hardener
prompts.sprintRole: Retrofit a repository's agent prompts, harness, workflows, ledgers, and validators so agents advance through explicit progress states, resume safely after interruption, and continuously converge independently green work into the default branch instead of stopping early or spinning
prompts.useWhen: A repository repeatedly produces agents that plan instead of execute, stop at commits or green PRs, leave merge-ready branches stranded, poll without changing state, lose context after interruptions, re-prove old work, or ask users to perform routine repository operations.
prompts.inspectFirst: Repository governance and context router; operational prompts/skills; work ledger/status vocabulary; branch/PR and merge-gate conventions; CI/workflow triggers; validators/tests; current main/open/recent PR history showing early-stop or stranded-green patterns; recovery artifacts; proof/acceptance contracts; and existing shared actionability or integration policies.
prompts.expectedOutput: The smallest durable loop contract placed in canonical owners, focused regressions that fail on early-stop/spin/stale-proof/stranded-green behavior, recovery and progress-state semantics, merge-forward enforcement, updated affected prompts without duplicating shared policy, generated artifact parity when applicable, and validated integration to main.
prompts.nextStep: Identify the highest-frequency early-stop or loop failure in current repository evidence, patch the narrowest canonical prompt/harness/validator owner that can prevent it, add a regression reproducing the failure, validate the connected surfaces, integrate the green prevention slice, refresh main, and iterate on the next proven failure only if it remains. Run the continuous agentic repo loop with P84; when agents emit brittle or wrong-shell commands, repair the Lua flagging and host enforcement loop with P90.
prompts.proofGate: The repository has an explicit non-spinning progress state machine; continuation states cannot terminate with generic status or a green unmerged PR; independently valid green slices converge to the default branch when gates permit; stale proof is invalidated by material movement; interrupted work resumes from durable evidence; user escalation is limited to genuine user-only gates; regressions exercise the observed failure modes; and the final prevention change is verified on current main.
prompts.copyContent:
HARDEN THIS REPOSITORY FOR CONTINUOUS AGENTIC LOOPS. FIX THE SYSTEM THAT MAKES AGENTS STOP EARLY, SPIN, LOSE STATE, OR LEAVE GREEN WORK UNMERGED. DO NOT JUST WRITE A BETTER ONE-OFF PROMPT.

Repo: resolve the current repository and actual default branch.
Observed failure: derive from the user's complaint and current repository evidence.
Owned scope: canonical agent prompts/skills/harness contracts, work-state/ledger semantics, focused validators/tests, workflow wiring, and generated Prompt Kit parity when those surfaces own the failure.
Forbidden scope: unrelated product rewrites, wholesale governance replacement, duplicated policy appendices, weakening checks, destructive cleanup, secrets/private data, or changing domain behavior merely to make the harness simpler.

MISSION
Turn recurring `the agent stopped` behavior into an executable repository contract. The hardened repository should make the easiest correct path:
REFRESH -> CHOOSE NEXT EXECUTABLE GATE -> ACT -> VALIDATE -> CRITIQUE -> INTEGRATE GREEN SLICE -> REFRESH -> CONTINUE.
Treat agentic looping as a consistency, recovery, and convergence problem, not as instructions to retry forever.

1. RECOVER THE FAILURE PATTERN
Inspect recent/current evidence for concrete loop failures: plan/status-only termination while executable work remained; stopping after code, commit, push, PR creation, review-ready state, green CI, or mergeability; green branches/PRs stranded instead of integrated; stale local/default-branch assumptions; repeated proof of already-established facts; repeated polling with no state change; branch multiplication instead of owner reuse; giant long-lived branches that postpone safe integration; interruption causing the next agent to restart or ask for context already recorded; routine tests/logs/review/merge work delegated to the user; moved heads treated as still validated; dependency order ignored; or proof claims exceeding observed evidence. Use actual repository/PR/CI history when available. Do not invent a failure merely to justify a new rule.

2. FIND THE CANONICAL OWNER
Before adding text, locate where the behavior should live. Prefer an existing shared actionability/integration policy if the rule is universal; the canonical repo-sprint/executor prompt for execution-loop specifics; an agent continuity/verifier/work-ledger prompt for handoff/resume specifics; a harness workflow/state contract for deterministic transitions; or a validator/test when the behavior can be machine-checked. Do not paste the same long doctrine into every prompt.

3. DEFINE A PROGRESS STATE MACHINE
Encode states in repository-native vocabulary. If none exists, model equivalent semantics such as READY -> ACTIVE -> VERIFY -> REVIEW -> INTEGRATE -> CONTINUE/DONE with BLOCKED/OPERATOR only for exact external gates. Every nonterminal state needs a current evidence floor, owner, one executable next action, an acceptance/exit gate, and durable proof from the last material transition. A state transition must change owned repository state, produce decision-relevant evidence, integrate validated work, or prove a blocker. Status restatement is not a transition.

4. SEPARATE PROGRESS LOOPS FROM RETRY LOOPS
A progress loop chooses and advances a new gate. A retry loop repeats a failed operation after a changed condition. Require a reason for retries and bound transient retries. Prevent commands/workflows from silently re-running unchanged failures forever. After retries are exhausted, record the exact external/system gate.

5. ENFORCE CONTINUOUS GREEN-SLICE CONVERGENCE
A branch/PR is a temporary lane. Add or strengthen the rule that independently coherent, exact-head-validated, review-clean, dependency-satisfied, merge-authorized work integrates into the current default branch in the same execution window. Do not require the entire broad mission to finish before merging a smaller independently valid slice. Do not split atomic migrations merely to merge more often. After each integration require current default-branch SHA resolution, proof that the slice is present, refreshed dependency/PR floor, downstream revalidation when base movement matters, and selection of the next remaining gate. A green PR that the agent is authorized and able to merge is a continuation state, not a blocker and not completion.

6. HARDEN RESUME / INTERRUPTION RECOVERY
Require durable checkpoints for material transitions: commit/merge SHA, PR, workflow run, artifact/hash, ledger task, or validation receipt. A new agent/session should refresh current remote/provider truth, recover the latest durable checkpoint, classify inherited proof as current/stale/partial, and resume at the first unproven gate. Do not force users to replay prior chats or reconstruct repository state that tools/ledgers can recover.

7. HARDEN FRESHNESS
Bind validation to exact head/base/dependency/input/artifact identities. Material movement invalidates only the proof it could affect; do not blindly restart all proof. Re-fetch before final integration. Preserve dirty/separately owned work instead of force-resetting to current main.

8. KEEP AGENT-CAPABLE WORK WITH THE AGENT
Prompts/harnesses must not use the user as a test runner, log collector, CI watcher, branch reconciler, generated-artifact builder, or routine merge operator when tools/permissions can perform those actions. User escalation requires a genuine user-controlled dependency and must happen only after independent safe work is exhausted.

9. ADD EXECUTABLE REGRESSIONS
For each observed failure you claim to harden, add the smallest focused test/validator/fixture that would fail if the behavior regresses. Useful checks include executor loop semantics; green+mergeable+authorized PR classified as merge-now; continuation states rejecting status-only next actions; moved-head proof invalidation; canonical generated-artifact parity; inherited completion claims requiring current evidence; recovery state containing durable checkpoint plus executable resume action; shared policy inheritance; and compact direct invariants for raw prompts that bypass policy injection. Static text cannot prove runtime model obedience, so keep the proof ceiling explicit.

10. ITERATE THE HARDENING ITSELF
Use at least two meaningful passes. PASS 1: implement the narrowest prevention for the highest-evidence failure and validate it. PASS 2: inspect the diff, generated artifacts, tests, current PR/base movement, and whether a weaker model could still stop at an intermediate state. Repair concrete gaps and revalidate. Continue only while evidence exposes a real defect.

11. INTEGRATE THE PREVENTION
When the hardening slice is exact-head green, review-clean, dependency-satisfied, mergeable, and authorized, merge it to the current default branch in the same run. Refresh main and verify the prevention exists there. If the original request includes more than one proven loop failure, select the next highest-value failure and repeat from current main rather than stacking indefinite unmerged hardening.

DELIVER
Report the observed agent-loop failures used as evidence; canonical owner(s) strengthened; prompts/contracts/validators/tests changed; state-machine and anti-spin rules installed; green-slice integration behavior installed; recovery/freshness behavior installed; focused regressions and connected validation actually run; generated-site parity when applicable; commit/PR/merge state and resulting default-branch SHA; proof ceiling; and next executable action or exact blocker.
